hints: Notice the arrow from X to Y in the diagram - the car starts near person P and moves away from P toward person Q at constant speed.
Connect motion to the Doppler effect - motion toward an observer shortens the observed wavelength and raises observed frequency $f_o$, motion away lengthens wavelength and lowers $f_o$.

walkthrough: Identify the geometry from the diagram: the car travels X to Y, so its velocity is directed away from person P behind it and toward person Q ahead of it, with constant magnitude.

State the Doppler rule for sound: observed frequency $f_o$ is higher than source frequency $f_s$ when source and observer are approaching, and lower than $f_s$ when they are receding, because wavefronts are crowded or spread in the direction of motion.

Apply to person P: the source recedes at constant speed, so the observed wavelength $\lambda_o$ is constantly larger than normal and $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ is constantly lower than $f_s$. It does not increase with time, so statement 1 is false.

Apply to person Q: the source approaches at constant speed, so $\lambda_o$ is constantly smaller than normal and $f_o$ is constantly higher than $f_s$. It does not decrease with time, so statement 2 is false.
Compare the two observers: for the whole journey Q receives the approaching-source frequency while P receives the receding-source frequency, so $f_Q > f_s > f_P$. Statement 3 is true.
Only statement 3 is correct, which matches the combination 3 only. This is option C.
